parsed.attack: The closest thing to an incumbent is Beeminder, which already ships the non-deferential mechanic as the akrasia horizon: you cannot change a goal inside seven days, and the record cannot be quietly rewritten. Adding a spoken check-in to that is not a large piece of work. Duolingo owns the evening-learner streak-pressure loop and has the distribution to put a voice commitment in front of this audience. But neither is a category leader that can make a product evaporate, and the platform owners who could are the ones structurally barred from shipping it.
parsed.strongest_defence: Apple, Google and OpenAI cannot ship a feature that refuses a paying user a silent edit to their own record. A general assistant's memory is user-editable by design, its default stance is reassurance, and an assistant that argued with the person paying for it would be a trust and support liability rather than a feature. The stance is not merely unshipped by incumbents, it is unshippable by them, and Beeminder's existing version of it has spent a decade without reaching scale, so it is not the thing that absorbs this.
parsed.verdict_reason: The product depends on refusing the user, which is exactly the stance the platform incumbents structurally will not take, so absorption is not the failure mode here.
